semrushOptimization._doc: Rules for achieving 9+/10 in Semrush SEO Writing Assistant. SWA scores 4 sub-categories: SEO, Readability, Tone of Voice, Originality. ALL must be optimized to hit 9+.

seo._note: After entering the target keyword in SWA, it generates ~20 recommended keywords from competitor analysis. ALL must be naturally incorporated — each missing keyword drags the SEO sub-score down.
seo.keywordInsertionStrategy: Weave each recommended keyword into existing sentences or add new content sections that naturally include them. Never keyword-stuff — each phrase should appear 1-2 times max.

internalLinks._note: SWA checks for links. In .mdx markdown links count when rendered but NOT when pasted as plain text into SWA. Still include them in the article.

readability._wordCountNote: SWA calculates a word count target based on top-10 competitor average. Article MUST meet or exceed this target. If SWA says 2,181, don't stop at 1,862.
readability._sentenceNote: Split any sentence over 25 words. SWA flags 'hard-to-read' sentences — the single biggest readability penalty. Split at conjunctions (and, but, or, which). Target 15-20 words per sentence.
readability._passiveNote: Convert ALL passive voice to active: 'penalties are assessed' → 'the IRS assesses penalties'. 'The FBAR must be filed' → 'You must file the FBAR'.
readability._paragraphNote: Split any paragraph over 4 sentences. Use bullet lists for requirements, steps, and lists of 3+ items.
readability._complexWordsNote: Replace multi-syllable words with simpler synonyms where meaning is preserved. Tax-specific terms (FBAR, FinCEN, CFR) are exempt — only replace general vocabulary.

toneOfVoice._toneNote: Tax compliance content should be 'somewhat formal' — professional but accessible. SWA measures consistency percentage. Every casual sentence in an otherwise formal article drags consistency down.
toneOfVoice._fillerNote: Replace 'add up' → 'total/sum', 'in order to' → 'to'. Remove the rest entirely or restructure the sentence.
avoidCasualPatterns: Sentence-fragment headings should still read as complete thoughts
Avoid question-only headings when a statement works ('Who Must File' → 'Filing Requirements by Person Type')
Don't start sentences with 'If the process feels...' or emotional appeals in instructional content
Replace colloquial phrases: 'a frequent surprise' → 'commonly overlooked', 'the good news' → omit or restructure
toneOfVoice._itIsNote: 'It is not filed...' → 'The FBAR is not filed...' or 'You do not file the FBAR...'. SWA flags 'it is' as an unnecessary placeholder.

originality._note: Always run the Copyleaks originality check in SWA before scoring. Unscored originality may cap the overall score. Paraphrase regulatory boilerplate — threshold amounts, filing deadlines, and legal definitions commonly match other FBAR articles online.
